claims.text: Vulnerability index (VI) should be defined as stress/strength and stress is best interpreted as the pulsatile amplitude ΔPSS (fatigue perspective), implying the need for pulsatile FSI simulations.
Vulnerability indices must normalize stress by fibrous-cap strength (E_fc^α); strength-normalization choice materially affects VI behavior.
Material properties dominate VI variability (Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology); key determinants are vessel wall stiffness, fibrous-cap stiffness, systolic blood pressure and pulse pressure.
Two selected VIs (VI1=ΔPSS/E_fc^0.5, VI2=ΔPSS/E_fc^1.0) satisfy all seven established clinical high-risk plaque criteria and show promising diagnostic separation (surrogate-evaluated).

warnings: claim_without_evidence: Vulnerability indices must normalize stress by fibrous-cap strength (E_fc^α); strength-normalization choice materially affects VI behavior.
evidence_without_provenance: GPR surrogate evaluation of VI2 shows diagnostic separation on synthetic high-risk label: AUC ≈0.84 (95% CI 0.80–0.88), Youden sensitivity ≈0.78, specificity ≈0.76
